candidates.attacker_control: The header is cleartext, prepended to ciphertext, and fully attacker-controlled. Callers documented to process untrusted ciphertext include CipherUtil.decrypt(BlockCipher/AEADBlockCipher, SecretKey, byte[]/InputStream/OutputStream) and AbstractCipherBean.decrypt(...) (bean/AbstractCipherBean.java:149-168), which call CiphertextHeader.decode(input) before any key lookup, decryption, padding or MAC check. A crafted byte array/stream of ~8-12 bytes controls nonceLen/keyLen arbitrarily.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the header-length field is validated (line 145: length < 0) but NonceLen and KeyNameLen are not. Confirmed the catch clauses (lines 155, 168, 200, 214) do not cover NegativeArraySizeException or OutOfMemoryError. Confirmed allocation happens before BufferUnderflowException can fire on bb.get(nonce)/bb.get(b), i.e. bounds checks are too late. Checked that the newer CiphertextHeaderV2 format deliberately stores NonceLen as a 1-byte unsigned value and caps the key name (CiphertextHeaderV2 lines 202-215), indicating these V1 4-byte length fields are the weak point; no caller-side length validation was found in CipherUtil or the bean classes. Not runtime-confirmed; no tests exist in the snapshot and no code was executed.
candidates.impact: Denial of service against any service that decrypts untrusted headers: large nonceLen/keyLen values force excessive heap allocation (OutOfMemoryError, potentially affecting all requests in the JVM), and negative values raise an uncaught NegativeArraySizeException instead of the declared EncodingException, potentially aborting request/thread handling. Both occur before any authentication, so no key or valid ciphertext is required.
candidates.prerequisites: An application uses CiphertextHeader-based decryption on data it does not fully trust (the class is explicitly designed for key rotation over outstanding ciphertexts). Default heap sizing applies; each malformed header can request a very large allocation. Byte[] path: lines 152-154 (nonce) and 164-166 (key name); stream path: lines 197-199 and 211-213.
candidates.root_cause: CiphertextHeader.decode() parses the cleartext header with only one validation: the total header length must be non-negative. The NonceLen and KeyNameLen fields are read as raw big-endian 4-byte ints (ByteBuffer.getInt / ByteUtil.readInt) and used directly as array sizes (new byte[nonceLen], new byte[keyLen]) before any comparison against remaining/available data. Negative values cause NegativeArraySizeException, which is not covered by the catch clauses (only IndexOutOfBoundsException | BufferUnderflowException, and IOException in the stream variant), and very large values request up to ~2 GB per request before any cipher/authentication step can reject the input.
candidates.title: Unbounded/negative array allocation from unvalidated CiphertextHeader length fields (decryption DoS)
candidates.trace: decrypt(byte[] data) -> CiphertextHeader.decode(data) -> bb.getInt() length (line 144, only checked for <0) -> bb.getInt() nonceLen (line 152) -> new byte[nonceLen] (line 153) -> bb.get(nonce) (line 154). If length > nonce.length + 8 (line 160): bb.getInt() keyLen (line 164) -> new byte[keyLen] (line 165) -> bb.get(b) (line 166). InputStream variant mirrors this at lines 197-199 (new byte[nonceLen], input.read(nonce)) and 211-213 (new byte[keyLen], input.read(b)). No upper bound and no cross-check against data length/stream length is performed at any point.
candidates.unverified: Actual allocator/heap behavior (OutOfMemoryError vs. VM survival), and whether deployed callers impose their own size caps, were not verified. The snapshot also contains undefined symbols in CiphertextHeaderV2 (MAX_KEYNAME_LEN, ByteUtil.toUnsignedByte/toString(byte[],int,int)/toInt(byte)), so the newer V2 path could not be fully assessed; this candidate is based solely on V1 code that is self-consistent.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-789 Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value / CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (improper input validation, CWE-20)

coverage_summary: Scope per get_source_scope: 131 model-visible files under the assigned root (src/main Java sources, pom/checkstyle/assembly config, README, two OpenSSL test artifacts); binaries are refused and no files were excluded by sensitive-name/path filters. Per get_relation_scope the P1 index covers all 131 files (no missing files, no hash mismatches; 985 symbols/1702 edges) but is explicitly syntactic navigation only, not data-flow, reachability, or a SAST result. I read all security-relevant areas in full: CiphertextHeader/CiphertextHeaderV2, CipherUtil, HashUtil, KeyPairUtil, PemUtil, NonceUtil, SaltedHash, BCryptHashBean, EncodingHashBean/SimpleHashBean, the ASN.1 key decoders, pbe schemes/algorithms, cipher/digest/codec specs, nonce generators, the codec package, x509/DN readers, and io stream wrappers; remaining adapter/wrapper and small support classes were skimmed (they contain no parsing or trust-boundary logic). Index facts (security_call/deserialization hints) were checked against source and are name-based navigation hints only. No build, tests, or scanners were run, and there are no test sources in the snapshot.
limitations: No code was executed and the project was not built; findings are source-level only and not runtime-confirmed.

The snapshot contains unresolved references inside CiphertextHeaderV2 (MAX_KEYNAME_LEN and three ByteUtil helpers) and private-field access from the subclass, so that file cannot compile and its effective runtime behavior (including any key-name length cap) could not be assessed.
No test sources or version history are present, so upstream intent (design weakness vs. regression) could not be confirmed.
Reachability of the vulnerable decode path depends on how consuming applications expose decryption; only in-repo callers were traced.
BouncyCastle provider internals (bcrypt cost validation, engine behavior) were not inspected, as the dependency is not in the source tree.

rejected_leads.lead: CiphertextHeaderV2.arraysEqual (lines 297-308) compares the recomputed HMAC with the attacker-supplied tag byte-by-byte with early return, a non-constant-time comparison (CWE-208) of an authentication value on untrusted headers.
rejected_leads.reason: Real code-quality/security smell, but practical exploitability of a 32-byte HMAC timing oracle through this API is uncertain, and the class is not used anywhere else in the snapshot (dead code in-tree). Lower impact than the header-allocation DoS.

rejected_leads.lead: CiphertextHeaderV2.decodeInternal references undefined symbols (MAX_KEYNAME_LEN at line 204; ByteUtil.toUnsignedByte at line 113; ByteUtil.toString(byte[],int,int) at line 209; ByteUtil.toInt(byte) at line 214), and writes to private parent fields (nonce/keyName/length are private in CiphertextHeader).
rejected_leads.reason: Source cannot compile as present, so effective bounds/behavior cannot be established; the intended key-name limit likely exists upstream. This is a snapshot-integrity limitation, not a demonstrable vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: BCryptHashBean.BCryptParameters (lines 263-276) parses cost with Integer.parseInt and no [4,31] range check (setCost enforces the range, compare does not); HashUtil.compareHash and BCryptHashBean.compare use early-exit byte comparisons.
rejected_leads.reason: Verification cost comes from the stored hash, normally trusted; BouncyCastle's BCrypt.generate may itself range-check cost. Timing differences are dominated by the expensive bcrypt/hash computation. Left unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: StreamCipherSpec.newInstance maps algorithm name "Grainv1"/"Grain-v1" to ISAACEngine (line 48) rather than a Grain engine; no Grainv1Engine import exists.
rejected_leads.reason: Silently substitutes a different cipher (correctness/interoperability problem with possible crypto-misuse implications), but source alone cannot establish a concrete attacker-driven security impact; may be a long-standing upstream mapping choice.

rejected_leads.lead: Short/empty input index errors: PemUtil.isPem reads data[0..63] and new String(data,0,10) without length checks (PemUtil.java:54-69); HexDecoder.decode calls input.get(0)/input.get(1) unconditionally (HexDecoder.java:40-41); CiphertextHeader negative lengths can throw NegativeArraySizeException.
rejected_leads.reason: These produce uncaught RuntimeExceptions (robustness/DoS edge cases) rather than memory exhaustion or data compromise; folded into the main candidate only where they share the unvalidated-length root cause.

rejected_leads.lead: NonceUtil.timestampNonce/nist80063a and RandomIdGenerator randomness characteristics (modulo bias, timestamp material).
rejected_leads.reason: Timestamp bytes are only DRBG personalization/nonce inputs combined with SecureRandom entropy, and the modulo bias is negligible; no security-relevant predictability was demonstrated.

summary: Reviewed the cryptacular 1.2.4-SNAPSHOT Java crypto library (131 model-visible source files) with P1 navigation only as a hint source. The strongest source-evidenced issue is in the cleartext ciphertext-header parser: CiphertextHeader.decode trusts attacker-controlled 4-byte NonceLen/KeyNameLen fields and allocates arrays of those sizes before any bounds check or authentication, giving a remote denial-of-service primitive on the decryption path (CWE-789/CWE-770). Several other leads (non-constant-time HMAC/mac comparison, unvalidated bcrypt cost, Grainv1 mapped to ISAAC, short-input index errors, and a snapshot-level inconsistency around CiphertextHeaderV2's undefined MAX_KEYNAME_LEN/ByteUtil helpers) were considered but are weaker or unverifiable; they are listed as rejected leads rather than additional candidates.
